lens: Aster: honesty surface and maintainer tooling
title: Blob Basis
tagline: Hash a file on every basis at once (on-disk, LF-normalised, CRLF-synthesised, committed git blob) and say which basis a recorded provenance hash was taken on, so OQ-17-7 stops recurring.
pitch: `node blob-basis.mjs <repo> <path>...` prints, for each path: on-disk sha256 and byte count; the blob id (`git rev-parse HEAD:path`) and the sha256 of `git cat-file blob` (the committed basis); `git hash-object` of the on-disk bytes; the LF-normalised and CRLF-synthesised sha256 of the on-disk bytes; the `.gitattributes` eol/text rule for the path; and a verdict: IDENTICAL, CRLF-CHECKOUT (LF-normalised equals the blob), or DIRTY. `--expect <sha256>` names the basis a recorded hash matches. `--scan <json>` walks a provenance JSON for 64-hex strings with a sibling `bytes` or `path` and reconciles each against the named file. Without git it degrades to the disk/LF/CRLF triad and says the blob basis is UNAVAILABLE. Run here: the horizons fixture's LF blob is `b278dd55…` at 7,214,102 bytes, equal to the screening cache's `provenance.horizonsFixtureSha256`; the CRLF synthesis is `c91f4e50da0e6fc5…` at 7,510,022 bytes (7,214,102 plus 295,920 newlines), exactly what `tools/slice12-research/data/earth-vz-span-max.json:8-9` pins, which is why that artifact cannot be reproduced from any clone.
whyNow: STATUS.md:452-461 (OQ-17-7 restated: 'Verify provenance against git cat-file blob, never against on-disk bytes'); `tools/build/precompute-lambert-screen.mjs:181` (`sha256Buffer(HORIZONS_BYTES)` over disk bytes); `tools/slice12-research/data/earth-vz-span-max.json:8-9` (sha256 c91f4e50…, bytes 7510022); audit `ASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md:318,554` and recommendation 13 (:501-502, re-pin on the committed-blob basis); STATUS.md:412-414 (docs/ on-disk bytes differ from served bytes because of `.gitattributes:9`); `mcp/scripts/bake-provenance.mjs` copies disk bytes into the package. All hashes above were computed in this session, not copied.
computes: Inputs: repo dir, paths, optional --expect, --scan. For each path: sha256(disk), sha256(disk with CRLF→LF), sha256(disk with LF→CRLF), bytes of each, blob id via git rev-parse HEAD:path, sha256(git cat-file blob), git hash-object --stdin of disk bytes, git check-attr eol text. Verdict logic: IDENTICAL if sha256(disk)==sha256(blob); CRLF-CHECKOUT if sha256(LF)==sha256(blob) and disk != blob; DIRTY otherwise; UNAVAILABLE for blob fields when git fails. --expect: matches the given hash against the four bases and prints the basis name or NO-MATCH. --scan: regex /[0-9a-f]{64}/ in JSON strings; uses a sibling 'path' or a --path override; prints a reconciliation table.
dataNeeded: Snapshot `tests/fixtures/v2/lambert-screen-cache.json` --pick metadata (1.2 KB; the provenance block) and `tools/slice12-research/data/earth-vz-span-max.json` --pick fixture (0.5 KB) as reconciliation targets; a 1 KB LF text fixture and its CRLF twin for unit tests. Under 5 KB. The real reconciliation runs against a live checkout and is skipped when absent.
existingOverlap: The bank's own `tools/snapshot.mjs` records blob id vs hash-object of read bytes for files it copies (a subset of this). Aster has no hashing helper; the generator and `measure-earth-vz.mjs` each hash disk bytes inline. Differs: a reusable basis report with a verdict, the --expect basis finder, and the --scan reconciler over provenance JSON.
honestyRisks: Declaring CRLF-CHECKOUT when the difference is something else: the verdict requires exact equality of the LF-normalised hash with the blob hash, else DIRTY. Hashes are always computed, never typed; the README's quoted hashes are regenerated by the test. The tool never rewrites a file or a provenance artifact. In a shallow or git-less environment it says UNAVAILABLE rather than inferring.
testPlan: Unit: CRLF synthesis of the LF fixture adds exactly the newline count in bytes; LF-normalising the CRLF twin reproduces the LF hash; a mixed-EOL fixture is DIRTY; --expect with the LF hash names 'lf'. Reconciliation (skipped without the checkout): sha256 of `git cat-file blob HEAD:src/v2/data/horizons-inner-solar-system-2026-2040.json` equals the snapshotted cache `horizonsFixtureSha256`; CRLF synthesis equals the snapshotted `earth-vz-span-max.json` sha256 and its bytes 7,510,022; --scan over the two snapshots yields one BLOB-BASIS match and one CRLF-BASIS match.
landing: Aster: `tools/provenance/blob-basis.mjs`; `precompute-lambert-screen.mjs:181` and `tools/slice12-research/measure-earth-vz.mjs` hash `git cat-file blob` bytes (or record both hashes with a `basis` field); re-emit `earth-vz-span-max.json` on the blob basis (audit item 13); close OQ-17-7 additively in `SLICE_17_FOUNDING.md`. `.gitattributes` normalisation (C1) is already done; this makes it checkable.
notes: Verified cache provenance.horizonsFixtureSha256 b278dd55… and STATUS OQ-17-7 hashing-basis restatement. Narrow but exactly the tool OQ-17-7 asks for.

Reproduced both hashes exactly: git cat-file blob sha256 b278dd55…=cache horizonsFixtureSha256 at 7,214,102 B; earth-vz-span-max.json pins c91f4e50… at 7,510,022 B (CRLF basis); closes OQ-17-7 with evidence.

earth-vz-span-max.json pins sha256 c91f4e50… and 7,510,022 bytes while the cache's horizonsFixtureSha256 is b278dd55…; STATUS:452-461 states OQ-17-7 in exactly these terms. Pure node:crypto plus git subprocesses; small and directly closes an open question's measurement half.
